decision.summary: 14S LMFP BMS Architecture Review: Proceed with shared-core architecture (STM32G474 + BQ79616-Q1 + shunt) pending cell datasheet and FuSa target resolution.
decision.recommendation: Adopt the BQ79616-Q1 AFE and STM32G474 MCU core paired with shunt-based coulomb counting and OCV-transition recalibration. Re-derive all voltage thresholds from the LMFP cell datasheet (discard LFP 3.65V limits), audit 48V legacy components for 60.2V max pack voltage, implement low-temperature charge inhibiting, and require a BMS-controlled charger handshake. Hold schematic freeze until cell datasheet, FuSa target, and peak current ratings are supplied.

assumptions.statement: LMFP cell max charge voltage is ≤4.2V (pack max 58.8V), maintaining SELV (<60V DC) low-voltage status.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If cell max voltage is 4.3V, pack voltage reaches 60.2V, exceeding SELV limits and triggering strict galvanic isolation and creepage/clearance safety standards.

assumptions.statement: Passive balancing via BQ79616 at ~40mA is sufficient for cell balance convergence across daily charge windows.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Slow balance convergence (~12.5h for 0.5Ah delta) causes cumulative cell imbalance and reduced usable pack capacity if cells are loosely graded.

assumptions.statement: Host MCU (STM32G474) will meet functional safety requirements without requiring a lockstep/ECC automotive safety MCU.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Selection of ISO 26262 ASIL-B/C or strict AIS-156 compliance late in design will force an MCU architectural redesign (e.g., NXP S32K3).

assumptions.statement: Charger accepts dynamic BMS power commands via CAN bus.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A BMS-unaware fixed CC-CV charger risks severe over-charging if an individual cell reaches OVP while total pack voltage remains nominal.

risks.description: Reusing LFP voltage thresholds (3.65V OVP) on LMFP chemistry limits pack usable capacity by 15-25% or risks cell overcharge.
risks.mitigation: Re-derive OVP, UVP, and charge taper voltage thresholds directly from the manufacturer's LMFP cell datasheet.

risks.description: Legacy 48V platform hardware (FET Vds, DC-DC Vin max, capacitors) degraded or destroyed by 14S LMFP top-of-charge voltage (58.8V–60.2V).
risks.mitigation: Perform a component-level voltage rating audit on all legacy 48V hardware for ≥65V operating margin.

risks.description: SoC drift on flat OCV plateau using legacy LFP lookup method leads to ±20–30% estimation error.
risks.mitigation: Implement current-shunt coulomb counting with periodic reset using the Mn/Fe OCV transition step (~4.05V) as a recalibration landmark.

risks.description: Charging below 0°C causes irreversible lithium plating and internal shorts.
risks.mitigation: Enforce autonomous low-temperature charge inhibition in firmware and AFE protection logic.

risks.description: Inrush current during main contactor/FET switch-on into motor controller DC-link capacitance welds contacts or damages FETs.
risks.mitigation: Implement dedicated pre-charge circuit and BMS-controlled sequencing based on load capacitance.

tradeoffs.option: Passive Balancing (BQ79616 Resistor Bleed) vs Active Balancing
tradeoffs.benefit: Significantly lower cost and complexity, fully integrated into BQ79616 AFE.
tradeoffs.drawback: Dissipates energy as heat and yields slow bleed rate (~40mA), requiring multi-session charge convergence for large mismatches.

tradeoffs.option: Back-to-Back MOSFET Disconnect vs Mechanical Contactor
tradeoffs.benefit: Eliminates high continuous coil holding current (aiding sleep budget) and enables independent charge/discharge control.
tradeoffs.drawback: Requires robust thermal dissipation design for continuous current and mandatory pre-charge logic.

tradeoffs.option: Platform Architecture Split (Shared Core MCU/AFE with Variant Comms) vs Universal Single Board
tradeoffs.benefit: Prevents industrial ESS requirement creep (20-yr life, Modbus) from inflating low-cost 3-wheeler EV BOM.
tradeoffs.drawback: Requires maintaining two separate PCB assembly variants.

evidence.claim: 14S LMFP voltage range spans 42.0V (14x3.0V empty) to 58.8V (14x4.2V nominal full) up to 60.2V (14x4.3V peak full).
LMFP OCV exhibits two distinct voltage plateaus (Fe region ~3.4V, Mn region ~4.05V) separated by a transition region.
BQ79616-Q1 is a 16-channel AFE utilized in a 14S configuration, requiring unused channels to be tied off per manufacturer guidance.
STM32G474 lacks integrated BLE, requiring an external power-gated BLE transceiver module for diagnostic connectivity.

next_actions: Supply the LMFP cell datasheet detailing cell OCV vs SoC curve, max/min voltage limits, continuous/peak current limits, and operating temperature charge/discharge windows.
Define the functional safety target and regulatory market (e.g., India AIS-156 vs ISO 26262 ASIL-B) to freeze MCU selection.
Audit all 48V legacy hardware (MOSFET Vds, DC-DC input range, capacitors, connectors) for safety margin at 60.2V max pack voltage.
Confirm charger communication protocol (CAN-bus dynamic control vs fixed CC-CV output).
Obtain continuous/peak pack current specifications and motor controller DC-link capacitance to size disconnect FETs/contactors and pre-charge resistor.
freeze_blockers: Missing LMFP cell datasheet prevents deriving safety-critical OVP/UVP thresholds and confirming whether max pack voltage remains strictly <60V SELV limit.
Undefined Functional Safety target (AIS-156 / ISO 26262) leaves host MCU choice (STM32G474) unvalidated against system safety requirements.
Unverified voltage margin on legacy '48V' platform components under 58.8V–60.2V top-of-charge conditions.
